active.description: Durable active-run truth says the job is currently executing or mid-loop.

blocked.description: Durable dependency or nonlaunch truth says the job is not safely runnable yet.

queued.description: Durable scheduler eligibility says the job is runnable now, including explicit run-now requests.

idle.description: The job is enabled but neither runnable now nor terminally complete/failed/ambiguous.

completed_once.description: A once job already completed for its durable slot and must not be surfaced as next work unless a new run-now request exists.

failed.description: Durable terminal truth says the job ended unsuccessfully or with a proof-bearing failure outcome.

ambiguous.description: Durable scheduler signals disagree, so operator surfaces must fail closed instead of guessing.

provenance_requirements.rule: Every derived operator-facing scheduler classification must preserve the durable source signal that caused it.

next_selection_policy.rule: What's next must select the earliest runnable durable candidate first, and only fall back to future scheduled candidates after non-runnable statuses are excluded.
